_comment: agent-fabric ADR-068 rule 7, command-recognition: the hook and guard modules tools/fabric/cli/checks.py admits although a comparison, regex or string test in them names a `commands` command instead of asking tools/fabric/cli canonical(). Each value says why the module cannot ask: what the name is there, if not a command in a Bash line. An entry admits the whole module, a later comparison in it included; an entry that admits nothing is lint's finding, so a module's entry leaves with the name.

recognisers.runtime/claude-code/hooks/review-bash-gu: names `fabric-secrets` in SECRET_PATH, a regex over the raw Bash line, quotes, substitutions and chained segments included, where a read of a secret must still match: canonical() reads the words of a parsed command and would not see one inside $(…) or a quoted string. The regex carries the dispatcher spelling `fabric secrets` beside it (round 1 of #546, F1), with a case for each in tests/fixtures/review-bash-guard-cases.json
names `gzcoord-inbox` in WATCH_MISSING, the text of the line that tells a session to arm its watch: the command the session is told to run, not a reading of one
recognisers.tools/fabric/guards/agent_fabric_dir_aut: compares `fabric-role` as the key of a git trailer line (declared_role, over `git interpret-trailers --parse`), not as a command in a Bash line
recognisers.tools/fabric/guards/commit_hooks.py: compares `fabric-role` as a git trailer key (_typed_role), and `fabric-sign` as the basename of git's gpg.program config value (post_commit): neither is a word of a Bash line canonical() could read
